overview: Candidates for the 34th Middlesex State Representative race, Paul Ruseau, Will Mbah, and Chris Oates, participated in a forum hosted by the Mystic Valley Voters Forum to discuss housing, racial equity, and state legislative priorities.

items.title: Candidate Introductions
items.summary: Candidates Will Mbah, Paul Ruseau, and Chris Oates introduced their professional backgrounds in municipal government, education policy, and international relations.

items.title: Affordability and Housing
items.summary: The candidates discussed solutions to the housing crisis, including rent stabilization, increasing the housing supply, and establishing a public state bank to fund community projects.

items.title: Racial Disparity
items.summary: The panel addressed systemic racial inequities by proposing restorative justice programs, transit-oriented development, and reforms to the state lottery revenue distribution formula.

items.title: Palestine and Local Investment Policies
items.summary: Mbah and Ruseau characterized Israel's actions in Gaza as genocide and supported local divestment ordinances, while Oates cited the need for an International Court of Justice determination before applying the legal term.

items.title: Immigration and ICE Agreements
items.summary: All three candidates expressed opposition to the state's 287(g) agreement with ICE and supported ending the sharing of local law enforcement data with federal immigration authorities.

items.title: Digital Security and Social Media
items.summary: The candidates criticized a state bill requiring identity verification for social media, citing concerns over data privacy for adults and potential impacts on LGBTQ youth.

items.title: Public Question and Answer
items.summary: Residents asked the candidates about vacancy taxes for second homes, medical technology innovation in Massachusetts, and specific state house bills regarding pension divestment from weapons manufacturers.
